positive.query: Create a career ladder for our 40-person engineering team with IC and manager tracks.
Our leveling guide just says good, strong, excellent at each level. Rewrite the level expectations so promotion decisions are consistent.
Define promotion criteria and a calibration process that ties to our career framework.

nearMiss.query: Write a job description for a senior product designer to post on our careers page.
Draft the annual performance review for my direct report based on these notes.
Build salary ranges for each of our levels using this survey data.

holdout.query: Titles are inconsistent across our sales teams. Build a leveling framework and map existing reps to it.

scenarios.task: Hypothetical facts: a 25-person customer success team has titles CSM, Senior CSM, and Lead CSM used inconsistently across two regions. Two managers. No existing framework, no pay bands yet. Design a career ladder with tracks, levels, dimensions, and level expectations, and explain how to map current people and run promotions.
scenarios.baselineFailure: The baseline produces a table of adjectives (good, strong, excellent) with years-of-experience requirements, no manager track equivalence, no calibration, and maps people by current title.
